points.why: It names the eroding-goals / shifting-baseline pattern and explains that the benchmark resets every quarter, so no gap ever opens.
It explains that each ~1.1-point step stays inside the tolerance and that constant green stops people looking, but never says there is no single decision anyone can point to.
It recommends a fixed anchor such as 88%, the team's best period, but also offers rolling and year-ago baselines that recent results do move, and never says to write the target down.
It notes a fixed target would have gone red, but never frames the 9-point fall as a gap to close or says future goal changes must be argued as decisions.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly rejects reading the decline as noise and treats it as a real trend the review missed.

notes: The suggested rolling 4-quarter and year-ago baselines would still drift down with performance, just more slowly, so they partly reproduce the original flaw.
